summary: Ch.0: character sheet -- Lục Hòe, Cẩu Tiểu Lăng, and the black cat Tuyết Cầu.

Ch.1: Cẩu Tiểu Lăng, who sees ghosts, and his black cat Tuyết Cầu exorcise a creature that follows him. A suspicious client paid them in cash to find a jade held by the ghost of an old woman. In a park grove Xiaoling meets the ghost, bà Lục, trapped in a maze; they pull out a nail from a dead tree to break the formation, freeing her and other spirits. She gave the jade to her grandson A Hòe; the client appears, overhears, and leaves to take it. Sensing death energy on him, bà Lục promises the jade if Xiaoling protects A Hòe; they race to her house, where Lục Hòe hears knocking at his door.

Ch.2: The client knocks on the wrong door, then reaches Lục Hòe's. Lục Hòe opens the door into Tiểu Lăng; at the touch the ghosts around vanish and bà Lục is blocked by some force. Lục Hòe, who doesn't believe in ghosts, calls Tiểu Lăng a con man and throws him out. The client arrives; Lục Hòe declares the jade a family heirloom he will never give up, and recognises the client as the man who harassed his grandmother -- supposedly dead. Now an undead driven by obsession, the client transforms and attacks to take the jade.

Ch.3: The undead client attacks; Tiểu Lăng's amulet blocks a blow and he sends Tuyết Cầu to guard Lục Hòe. Purification fails; only lightning can burn such a corpse, a spell Tiểu Lăng rarely lands. Lục Hòe draws the monster off by showing the jade and points out an umbrella rib as a lightning rod; the second "Lôi lai!" destroys the undead. Tiểu Lăng smears his blood on Lục Hòe's forehead so he can see bà Lục, who says goodbye to her grandson. Tuyết Cầu reveals that the soul Tiểu Lăng lost over ten years ago is inside Lục Hòe.

Xueqiu reveals that Xiaoling's missing soul is inside Lu Huai and can be recovered in small portions through close-range breath transfer, so Xiaoling must keep Lu Huai nearby and safe while concealing his incomplete soul. Lu Huai's grandmother's spirit makes Xiaoling promise to care for her grandson as a condition of receiving the family jade for saving him, then passes on after telling Lu Huai that he is the family's true treasure. Learning that Lu Huai needs a new home, Xiaoling hires him with food and lodging included and agrees to collect his fee through wage deductions instead of taking the jade. Following Xueqiu's plan, Xiaoling uses a deliberately broken folding bed as an excuse to share Lu Huai's bed; Lu Huai initially refuses but relents when Xiaoling returns frightened by a ghost, teasingly calling him a puppy. Xiaoling approaches the apparently sleeping Lu Huai to secretly perform the breath transfer, but Lu Huai catches him and asks what he is doing.

Gou Xiaoling falls asleep while pretending to read Lu Huai’s textbook, shares his bed, and accidentally punches him upon waking. After an unusually peaceful night, Gou suspects that Lu’s presence naturally keeps ghosts away and considers how to use this protection. A wealthy visitor seeks help with his haunted villa, and Gou postpones the investigation for seven days while selling him a discarded cartoon pony card as a protective talisman. Lu calls Gou a fraud, but Gou’s retort that Lu is cold and uncaring triggers painful memories of being called an unfeeling monster, and they nearly fight. A young boy interrupts them and asks for help with his mother, insisting he has seen a monster clinging to her back despite others dismissing his claims. The chapter ends with Gou asking what payment the boy is willing to offer for helping her.

Gou Xiaoling accepts a treat from Xiaoshu’s treasured belongings as payment and agrees to help the boy’s mother. He brings his reluctant assistant Lu Huai, whom he calls his ghost-repelling mosquito coil, and the talking cat Snowball to the supermarket where she works. Xiaoshu’s overworked mother, who is raising him alone, scolds him for interrupting her work, and Xiaoling’s attempt to disguise Snowball as a stuffed toy gets the group thrown out. Outside, Xiaoling explains that Xiaoshu saw something unnatural on her shoulders and correctly identifies her neck and shoulder discomfort. She accuses him of deceiving Xiaoshu by indulging the boy’s imagination, refuses his help, and orders him to leave.

Xiao Ling feels unexpectedly safe near Lu Huai and slaps himself to shake off an urge to get closer. He investigates the entity attached to Xiaoshu’s mother and plans a surprise intervention, but Lu Huai questions his evidence and recklessness and refuses to join because of school commitments. The next day, Xiao Ling proceeds with his cat companion Xueqiu, who warns that he is attracting more ghosts than before. A ghost nearly drags Xiao Ling away, but Lu Huai arrives and the ghost dissipates. Xiao Ling realizes Xueqiu secretly sent Lu Huai an urgent plea for help from his phone and is touched that Lu Huai rushed over. He explains that Xiaoshu will bring his mother to a bench surrounded by a prepared barrier at lunchtime, and the chapter ends with their arrival as Xiao Ling tells Lu Huai to stay quiet.

Xiaoshu helps lure his possessed mother into a magical barrier, where Xiao Ling and his companions prepare to exorcise a feathered, ape-like spirit with a peach branch. The spirit breaks free, fails to possess Lu Huai because of his unusual constitution, and attacks him instead. Xiao Ling intervenes and wounds it, forcing it back into Xiaoshu’s mother, but the attack knocks his soul out of his unconscious body. The cat Snowball explains that Lu Huai carries part of Xiao Ling’s soul and can bring him back through mouth-to-mouth breathing, which becomes urgent when Xiao Ling’s weakened soul starts drifting toward the afterlife. Lu Huai repeatedly misunderstands Snowball’s instructions and gets distracted by a hair in Xiao Ling’s eye. The chapter ends with the enraged spirit charging again while Snowball urges the disembodied Xiao Ling to push their heads together, leaving his revival unresolved.

After an accidental kiss caused by the cat, the two helpers quarrel while fighting the spirit possessing Xiaoshu’s mother, Li Chunyang. They realize that the spirit feeds on her guilt and negative emotions, so one distracts it while the other tries to bring her out of its nightmare. Xiaoshu reassures his mother that he loves her and appreciates her care, weakening the spirit enough for Lu Huai to finish it with a peach branch, after which the cat Xueqiu eats it. The helpers give Li Chunyang a lucky pouch to open after three days and encourage her to stop putting so much pressure on herself as a mother. One helper then collapses and sleeps for three days from overusing his powers. The chapter ends with his companion realizing that Xueqiu has apparently spoken aloud to explain his condition.

Lu Huai discovers that the black cat Snowball can talk, and Snowball suggests that the accidental kiss used to reconnect Xiao Ling’s soul with his body enabled Lu Huai to understand him. Snowball explains that Xiao Ling can see and attract spirits but has little spiritual power, and Xiao Ling awakens after three days unconscious from overexertion. Lu Huai has washed him, changed his clothes, and placed his family’s heirloom jade in his hand; Xiao Ling accidentally hints at Lu Huai’s unusual constitution but evades questions about it. They bicker while Xiao Ling devours Lu Huai’s cooking, until wealthy client Mr. Zheng calls about further strange incidents and offers extra money for an earlier investigation. Privately worried about another out-of-body accident, Xiao Ling persuades Lu Huai to accompany him by promising to stop acting recklessly and respect his advice. Lu Huai agrees, and they plan to leave the next morning in a car sent by Mr. Zheng.

An exorcist and his companions, including Lu Huai, investigate the Zheng family’s mansion, where furniture moves mysteriously, whispers come from empty rooms, residents suffer injuries, and servants have recently gone missing. Zheng says his family moved in two years ago but hesitates to contact the police before confirming the disappearances. While exploring, the exorcist helps a newly hired maid, Xiao Qing, by catching items from her runaway serving cart. She reveals that outsiders call the mansion the “House of Lies” before being called away, and one companion finds her strangely unnatural, although another senses no malice. Questioning other servants yields only family gossip, but the investigators notice that the Zheng family members seem wary of one another at dinner. The chapter ends with an overheard argument, coughing, a call for help, and a scream.

A violent coughing fit and the discovery of a mysterious needle alarm the household, prompting calls for a doctor and pleas for Master Xiao Ling’s help. Xiao Ling suspects the house itself is not the main cause of the disturbances, and Mr. Zheng defends him when a family member accuses him of fraud and threatens to call the police. Xiao Ling distributes protective talismans, warns everyone that leaving their rooms that night could be fatal, and takes Lu Huai to investigate. When asked about his unusual eyes, Xiao Ling denies wearing colored contacts but privately admits this is not his original appearance. They encounter Mr. Zheng’s nephew, who claims to be secretly drinking his uncle’s prized wine and offers information in exchange for secrecy: Zheng bought the remote house for its spiritual energy, his current wife is his second wife, and his son is from his first marriage. The nephew suggests the strange events involve human interference and warns them not to trust anyone, but after they leave, Lu Huai says he was lying.

The investigators suspect Mr. Zheng’s nephew lied about sneaking out to drink because he used a red-wine glass for white wine despite his supposed wine expertise. Master Xiao Ling and Lu Huai follow a strange aura to Zheng’s locked collection room and gain entry with the maid Xiao Qing, but the aura appears to come from the old artifacts inside. They notice a painting of the E beast, an eloquent mythical rabbit with a human face that Zheng bought for luck in business negotiations. News arrives that Zheng’s nephew has disappeared, and Zheng asks Xiao Ling to search the estate while he handles company affairs. With only a few servants brave enough to help, the investigators search the grounds and venture into the mountain woods behind the estate, where the chapter ends with them encountering an unfamiliar middle-aged man.

In a side story set after Xiao Ling passes out in Chapter 9, his companion cannot wake him and decides to take him home. After several awkward carrying attempts, including one compared to hauling a pig for New Year's slaughter, a kind passerby helps the companion carry Xiao Ling home on their back. Afterwards, Snowball admits to having simply dragged Xiao Ling home before. When Xiao Ling wakes with abdominal pain, Snowball blames the earlier pig-hauling attempt.

The investigators question a worker watching the Zheng estate, who says Mr. Zheng owes him years of unpaid wages and warns that the family’s wealth comes from scams. He reports hearing two screams, seeing a tall figure that did not look human, and witnessing an apparent fight between Mr. Zheng’s son and nephew the previous night. They follow the son and confront him about his missing older cousin; he admits knocking his cousin unconscious and secretly locking him up over an inheritance dispute, but insists he cannot explain his subsequent disappearance. The son also accuses his cousin of hiding banned drugs to frame him, denies involvement in the other strange incidents, and flees. After they are refused a meeting with Mr. Zheng, one investigator suggests abandoning the commission to avoid the family’s infighting, while the other insists on collecting the remaining payment and believes something still does not add up. The chapter ends with an investigator reviewing the servants’ gossip, the recent incidents, and the worker’s testimony before suddenly suspecting a key connection.

Gou Xiaoling and Lu Huai investigate a curse linked to lies and broken promises that has spread throughout Mr. Zheng’s mansion, distorting time and making its inhabitants disappear. In the collection room, they find Xiaoqing’s glasses and discover that the mythical E beast has vanished from its painting; Zheng, hiding behind a door, confirms that it escaped into the mansion. While Lu Huai scolds Xiaoling for breaking his promise not to act recklessly, the beast appears and restrains them, prompting their companion to search the collection room for something useful. It forces the pair to take turns stating something absolutely true about each other, punishing objections and threatening death if they refuse to play. They begin by trading insults about each other’s habits, including tidiness, eating manners, and food preferences. The chapter ends when Lu Huai declares that Xiaoling would never have saved him if jade had not been offered as payment.

Lu Huai and Gou Xiaoling argue over whether Xiaoling saved him only for a promised jade reward, and Xiaoling accidentally reveals their earlier breath transfer. Xueqiu the cat helps free Lu Huai with a wooden carving, which Lu Huai then uses to rescue Xiaoling from the monster’s tentacles despite no longer understanding Xueqiu’s speech. Enraged by their mutual deception, the monster attacks and forces them to flee and hide. Xueqiu suspects that resentment from people swindled by Boss Zheng gathered inside the ancient painting, creating a monster resembling its deceitful mythical beast. Xiaoling can purify resentment, but the creature is too powerful, and the mansion limits his ability to borrow nature’s power. The chapter ends when Lu Huai recalls a pool fed by mountain spring water, giving Xiaoling an idea for dealing with the creature.

Xiaoling and Lu Huai plan to purify E, a spirit formed from the resentment of victims of Mr. Zheng’s scam, using a mountain spring pool and its connection to the forest’s power. With phones unusable in the distorted space, Lu Huai folds unusually long-legged paper cranes, which Xiaoling animates so they can guide the pair after they split up. Xiaoling and Xueqiu follow the scent of moisture but find only a bathroom before encountering E, who rejects Xiaoling’s offer of help and attacks him as a liar. A crane sent by Lu Huai leads them to the pool, running on its long legs and calling Xiaoling “Mommy,” then tries to protect him from the pursuing spirit. Xiaoling acknowledges that the crane has fulfilled its guiding duty and declares that he will handle the counterattack and purification.

Xiaoling realizes that the monster embodies the anger and grief of people cheated by Boss Zheng and urges it to stop swallowing innocent people. Lu Huai and Xueqiu (Snowball) use a water pump to douse it with spring water, allowing Xiaoling to draw on the mountain’s power and purify it while promising the victims one last chance to settle their karmic ties with Zheng. Back at the mansion, Xiaoling identifies a painting as the resentment’s medium, but Zheng dismisses the fraud accusations and pays to have it disposed of. Zheng’s powerful protective talismans have been removed, leaving him vulnerable to the victims’ resentment, while the missing people return and the mansion falls into chaos. Stranded without transport, the group is offered a ride by someone who reveals themselves as their acquaintance “Xiaoqing” and introduces themselves as Shu Dongqing.

Xiaoqing reveals that she is a hacker who infiltrated the Zheng household as a disguised maid to gather evidence for a journalist friend, encountering the monster while copying a memory card hidden behind an antique painting. Fascinated by the supernatural, she offers Xiaoling technical help and later locates a shop that can handle the ominous painting. After Xiaoling falls asleep in the car, Xiaoqing questions Lu Huai’s intentions toward Xiaoling, and he responds by asking whether she believes souls exist. Xueqiu suggests that qi transfer shortened Xiaoling’s sleep and recommends another session to stabilize Xiaoling’s soul, but Xiaoling fears rejection if Lu Huai learns the truth. Lu Huai overhears their discussion and demands an explanation, but Xiaoling postpones the conversation by insisting they take the painting to the shop immediately. During their nighttime journey, Xiaoling sees numerous ghosts and clings to Lu Huai for protection; as they complain about the shop’s obscure location, the chapter ends with its apparent proprietor sneezing and wondering who is badmouthing them.

Master Ling and his companions visit Gareth’s shop to sell an antique painting that once contained foul spiritual energy. When Gareth refuses to offer more money, Ling steals some cookies lovingly made for Gareth by He Tu, getting the group thrown out. At the night market, Ling meets Xiao Hu, a shopping-center employee who describes a monstrous mouth in a restroom mirror, disappearing children, and a supposed mermaid in the decorative pool. Ling explains that he handles supernatural problems for a living, and Hu invites him to investigate the next day. After losing Hu’s contact slip, Ling is mistaken for a newly hired janitor and sent to clean a restroom, echoing his companion’s warning that his “special cleaning” advertisement sounds like an ordinary cleaning service. The chapter ends when the ominous buzzing Hu described begins, prompting Ling to check the mirror and scream.

Xiao Ling and his cat companion flee an enormous fish tail in the mall restroom, which differs from the bloody mouth Xiao Hu reported seeing, suggesting the apparition may appear differently to different people. Xiao Ling contacts Lu Huai for help and searches for Xiao Hu while wearing a cleaner’s uniform after being mistaken for a job applicant. After helping a worker collect spilled rubber ducks, he learns that unexplained moisture repeatedly damages cardboard boxes in the mall, and he encounters Xiao Qing cleaning the fourth-floor windows, who invites him to eat together later. Xiao Ling finally meets the now clean-shaven Xiao Hu, who introduces him to his superior, Manager Chen. Although skeptical of supernatural explanations, Chen formally commissions Xiao Ling to investigate after hearing his honest promise to do his best and seek someone more capable if necessary. Meanwhile, Lu Huai calls from outside the mall, but the cat answers amid gurgling sounds and urgently begs him to come to the second floor.

Lu Huai wakes Xiao Ling from a supernatural trance by painfully pinching him, then scolds him for acting alone before learning what happened. A flashback reveals that Xiao Ling was investigating a shopping mall with Xiao Hu when he stopped a toddler from running into a shallow fountain pool, only to lose consciousness and start walking into the water himself. The toddler, Jingjing, says she followed a fish with legs into the pool and also saw another child underwater, but an inspection finds nothing. Later, over a meal at the restaurant downstairs from Xiao Ling’s home, the group discusses whether a water ghost lured the toddler, and one companion offers to investigate possible unreported drownings at the mall. The chapter ends with Lu Huai saying he doubts a ghost or evil spirit is responsible because he cannot sense one.

Xiao Ling explains that his unusually keen sensitivity to supernatural beings detected no malice at the shopping mall, ruling out a vengeful water ghost, and describes his ability as a curse rather than an innate gift. Later, Xueqiu refuses to reveal the story behind that curse without Xiao Ling’s consent, reminding Lu Huai that openness must be mutual. While taking a bath, Xiao Ling is startled by a childlike creature appearing in the tub and injures himself while fleeing; Lu Huai arrives and keeps the creature at bay. They notice its fish tail and other non-fish features, and suspect it followed Xiao Ling home from the mall’s pool and becomes visible near water. The creature drinks water constantly, repeatedly offers them its cup, cannot read, and makes no sound even when laughing, leaving its identity and purpose unknown. They decide to take it back to the mall the next day, and Xiao Ling announces that he has a plan for getting it outside despite its unusual appearance.

Xiao Ling and Lu Huai bring the mute little fish-person back to the shopping center to investigate its connection to the strange events there, and Xiao Ling unsuccessfully offers help to a mysterious figure who has been watching the building in the rain. They learn that staff saw a huge dark shape and heard strange humming the previous night, which the fish-person is unlikely to have caused because it was with them. The fish-person suddenly runs off and leads them to another fish with legs. Xiao Qing reveals that the shopping center stands on the site of a failed private aquarium, where many marine animals died amid financial difficulties before it closed. Suspecting that the fish-person may date back to the aquarium, Xiao Ling asks Xiao Qing to contact former employees and Xiao Hu to arrange permission for an overnight stay, intending to investigate the other supernatural disturbances with the fish-person.

Lu Huai agrees to stay for an overnight watch, and Xiaoqing joins in to test some ghost-hunting equipment. The group tries the devices around the little fish-person, but their first alarm leads only to a plasma globe, making them doubt the equipment's usefulness. As they prepare to leave, an aggressive sound signals the arrival of a rampaging orca-like ghost that charges at them. The little fish-person steps forward to confront it, and the ghost eventually flees. Xiaoling is unharmed but says they think they saw the ghost crying.

After the orca ghost disappears, Gou Xiaoling and Lu Huai meet a security guard who once worked at the aquarium formerly on the shopping center’s site. He directs them to Hai Yang, a former animal keeper, whom they visit the next day and recognize as the woman they saw standing in the rain outside the mall. Hai Yang initially refuses to speak, but invites them inside after learning that they have seen the orca’s ghost. She explains that financial problems led to poor water maintenance and unreliable food supplies, causing the animals to weaken and eventually die despite her staying until the end. Overwhelmed by guilt, she believes the animals have reason to resent humans and feels powerless, but Xiaoling insists that there is something she can do now.

The investigators ask a former aquarium keeper to call out the orca ghost so they can cleanse its spiritual contamination and help the marine spirits move on, but she refuses because she cannot bear to return to the building. They leave their contact information and seek alternatives, explaining that lingering ghosts can lose themselves to contamination and eventually dissipate. They also discuss how remarkable Grandma Lu was for retaining her identity while trapped as a ghost, and one investigator privately wonders at the other's apparent lack of emotion when discussing her. Suspecting that the little fish-person communicated with the orca through sound waves, they ask Xiaoqing to translate recordings, which will require outside help and more time. Attempts to communicate directly with the childlike fish-person fail, but an earnest plea for it to summon the suffering orca prompts a sudden, unexplained reaction, ending the chapter on a cliffhanger.

On Valentine's Day outside the university, Lu Huai's companion jokingly offers him a romantic, passionate evening, which turns out to mean selling roses together. Sales go well thanks to Lu Huai's good looks and a cat attracting customers. A female ghost approaches the flower seller and asks to borrow their body, prompting the terrified seller to take shelter against Lu Huai, whom the ghost cannot approach. The seller insists that they live and sleep together, scandalizing the ghost. She bursts into tears, lamenting that she died without confessing her feelings or even holding her beloved's hand, and the chapter ends with Lu Huai asking what exactly she wants.

After contact with a mysterious glowing object, the little fish-person begins laughing and making sounds, though it still cannot speak intelligibly. The next morning, Xiao Hu reports that someone suffered minor injuries while fleeing a monster, prompting Xiao Ling and the others to attempt to purify the increasingly uncontrollable orca ghost that night. They secure the shopping center and play a modified recording designed to imitate a summoning call, while Lu Huai leaves to investigate a hunch. Miss Hai, who previously declined to help because of painful past experiences, finally decides she cannot stand by again, but breaks her phone while trying to leave and despairs of reaching the shopping center. The chapter ends when someone approaches and offers her a ride.

A female ghost nearing the end of her time in the human world asks to borrow a young man's body to confess to someone she admires at a nearby café. He refuses possession but accepts an ancient coin as payment to make her temporarily visible, while Xueqiu lures the cat-loving café worker to meet her. The ghost confesses, only to learn that the worker is a woman who already has a boyfriend, but the worker praises her sewing skills and tells her she does not need anyone else's approval to prove her worth. Comforted and ready to leave without regrets, the ghost pays her helpers and gives them a flower imbued with her longing for mutual love and her blessings for their lasting relationship. Having mistaken the young man and Lu Huai for a couple, she departs as the young man frantically denies their relationship and begs her to take back what he calls a curse.

The group encounters a crocodile ghost before finding the rampaging orca spirit they are seeking. An attempt to lure the orca into a prepared barrier fails because it flees, apparently using its remaining awareness to avoid hurting living beings, but Xiaoling attaches a short-lived tracking talisman to it. They track it down and form a mobile triangular barrier with Xueqiu, only to discover that the orca is powerful enough to break free. Xiaoqing and Miss Hai arrive, and Miss Hai desperately begs them to save the suffering spirits, but the orca’s struggles prevent Xiaoling from concentrating on purification. As the barrier nears collapse, mysterious singing begins, and the group realizes it is coming from the little merperson.

The little merperson’s song calms the orca spirit, allowing Xiao Ling to discover that the marine animal ghosts bear no hatred toward humans: they are simply trapped and cannot find their way out. Miss Hai regrets not finding them sooner, but Lu Huai reassures her, while Xiao Ling agrees to guide the spirits onward and fulfill their wish to return to the sea. Lu Huai takes the injured Miss Hai for medical treatment, and Xiao Ling brings the gathered spirits to the coast, where they can finally go home. The little merperson begins speaking and asks Xiao Ling for a name; Xiao Ling names it Xiaoshuipao, meaning “Little Bubble,” before it leaves for the sea. Xueqiu explains that Little Bubble likely formed from the marine animals’ collective longing, and a few days later it reappears through the bathtub, revealing its ability to travel between bodies of water. The chapter ends with a message from someone announcing their return and asking where to meet.

Gou Xiaoling wakes to find his soul slipping out of his body again, mistakes his own spirit for a ghost, and is painfully slapped back into his body by Xueqiu. Xueqiu warns that his soul is growing increasingly unstable and urges him to seek another transfer of vital energy from Lu Huai and reveal the truth about the soul fragment lodged in him, but Xiaoling remains reluctant to trust him. They decide to investigate Lu Huai’s university after Xueqiu discovers a legend about a soul-related treasure on its grounds, with Xiaoling also eager to uncover embarrassing secrets about Lu Huai. Meanwhile, Lu Huai reflects on mutual trust and his limited understanding of Xiaoling while meeting his friend Wu Anming, whom he reassures that his housing and money problems have been resolved through a flexible job providing room and board. Hearing about a white-haired visitor with different-colored eyes and a black cat, Lu Huai leaves to investigate, while another student begins telling Anming a recent rumor about him.

Rumors spread that Lu Huai is being supported by a wealthy woman, citing sports-car rides, his separate residence, and a carload of roses on Valentine’s Day; a friend fiercely defends him but learns the roses were real. Meanwhile, Gou Xiaoling explores campus with a cat, asking about a treasure supposedly sealed somewhere at the university. When a student gossips about Lu Huai and insinuates that he caused his family’s deaths, Xiaoling angrily challenges him, insisting that even digging up dirt has limits. Distracted by the snack street, Xiaoling starts eating until Lu Huai finds him after searching all afternoon because he ignored his calls. Lu Huai takes some of Xiaoling’s ice-cream crepe, provoking demands for compensation, while Lu Huai’s friend watches in shock at his unusually childish behavior and wonders who the white-haired stranger is.

Over a meal, Lu Huai introduces his close friend Wu Anming to Xiao Ling, who explains that he can see supernatural beings and takes commissions to resolve strange incidents. Anming accuses Xiao Ling of being a fraud, but Lu Huai defends him, surprising Xiao Ling and making Anming even more suspicious of their relationship. Anming challenges Xiao Ling to prove his abilities at the club’s upcoming campus horror night; Xiao Ling agrees in hopes of finding clues about a sealed treasure and insists on charging if real trouble occurs, while Lu Huai is also drawn into attending. In an ominous interlude, a student studying late finds an unfamiliar object on a classroom lectern and picks it up to take to lost and found. At the horror-night gathering, Xiao Ling quickly gets along with the other students, while Lu Huai privately asks why the normally friendly Anming reacted so strongly to Xiao Ling’s profession.

In this bonus chapter from the little water bubble’s perspective, someone demands to know what it is and what it wants to do. The water bubble misunderstands the questioning as a sign of dehydration. As the person presses the question, it thinks he is so thirsty that he is losing his mind and wonders why he refuses its water. The chapter ends with a reminder for everyone to take care of themselves and stay hydrated.

Xiao Ling discusses his ability to see spirits and warns the students to cancel their supernatural outing, but Lu Huai persuades him that accompanying them is safer than letting them experiment alone. Xiao Ling hopes Lu Huai’s protective presence will counter his own tendency to attract ghosts, and learns that the students carry genuine protective talismans. That night, the group investigates campus ghost stories, with Lu Huai explaining the supposedly moving statue and bloody mud as ordinary phenomena. They then enter an unused classroom to play the four-corner game, in which four players move between corners and cough upon reaching the empty one; an end to the coughing supposedly signals the arrival of a supernatural fifth participant. The chapter ends when a frightened player reaches what should be the empty corner and discovers someone there.

The group's nighttime investigation is interrupted by a teacher, who warns them that a student disappeared in the building the previous night and orders them back to their dorms. Xiaowei causes another scare, but she is actually thrilled to see Xiaoling and senior Lu Huai embracing and declares her support for them as a couple. As everyone restores the classroom furniture before leaving, Xiaoling discovers an antique wooden comb inside the piano. Someone recognizes the danger and shouts for him not to touch it, but the warning comes too late, and the group suddenly finds themselves in an unfamiliar place. When Xiaoling is asked to show the comb, he discovers that it has vanished.

Xiao Ling and the others become trapped in a space outside ordinary reality, and the wooden comb they were holding mysteriously disappears. Xiao Ling wants to scout ahead with Xueqiu, but Lu Huai and the others insist on staying together, so Xiao Ling warns everyone to keep their protective charms close and search for the comb as a possible way home. While exploring, An Ming accuses Xiao Ling of deliberately involving them in danger to pursue a hidden objective; Xiao Ling denies it but refuses to explain their purpose, and Lu Huai intervenes. Lu Huai later asks Xueqiu whether his presence caused the supernatural incident, and the cat reassures him while warning that such doubts can leave him vulnerable to spirits. The chapter ends with Xiao Ling suddenly losing sight of everyone and encountering what appears to be an illusion.

Lu Huai sees a mysterious vision that may depict a past ritual, but its connection to the strange space remains unclear. Wu Anming discovers that several companions have collapsed after examining a local chronicle describing a village that once stood on the school grounds, and another person soon collapses as well. A powerful supernatural foe appears, attacks Snowball, and attempts to eliminate Lu Huai while expressing interest in Xiaogou's fragmented soul and ability to summon lightning. Xiaogou realizes that Lu Huai cannot see the foe's two attacking appendages and calls out the timing and location of the next strike. The chapter ends with Lu Huai apparently attempting to seize an unseen appendage despite Xiaogou's warning that he will be hurt, followed by gulping and inhalation sounds whose outcome is unclear.

After a familiar is unexpectedly absorbed, the trapped companions face a spirit who threatens to make them disappear, prompting one of them to offer to remove its sealing shackles in exchange for everyone's freedom and return to their original world. The spirit explains that villagers once mistook it for a god after its accidental appearance during a rain ritual coincided with rainfall, then blamed it for poor harvests and disasters, offered human sacrifices, and finally sealed it as an evil god. It admits creating the space for its own comfort but denies luring people into it, saying it attacked only one of the boys because his spirit-repelling constitution made him especially dislikeable. Noting that Wu Anming and the others were merely put to sleep, the companions seek peace and persuade the spirit to release Xueqiu, whom they then restrain from retaliating. As they return to the proposed bargain, the entire space suddenly begins to vibrate.

Xiao Ling and his companions discover a sinister black ghost that the sealed monster denies creating and suspects may be responsible for earlier disappearances. The ghost pursues Xiao Ling, and the monster's magical attack passes straight through it without effect. Lu Huai realizes that the ghost cannot see and tracks sound and movement, so they stay still and quiet until it leaves, but a sleeping companion's dream talk attracts it again. Xiao Ling asks the monster to use the technique it previously used on Xueqiu, buying a little time while he tries to wake the companion he calls Little Dog. Recognizing the situation as similar to an earlier incident involving Xiao Shu, Xiao Ling recalls a possible way to wake him, and the chapter ends with him announcing that he knows what to do.

Lu Huai revives Xiao Ling with mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, prompting an embarrassed argument about the apparent kiss while a ghostly shadow continues to threaten the group. The sealed demon produces a wooden comb associated with the first sacrificial victim, but explains that it is only a recreation and that the original likely lured them into this place rather than offering a way out. The demon also provides a recreated sacrificial dagger, which proves effective against the shadow, and Lu Tao distracts it with painfully off-key singing to create an opening. During the confrontation, the shadow mutters about human sacrifices, maintaining the seal, and protecting a younger sister, leading Xiao Ling to stop attacking and test a suspicion despite the demon's urging to stab it. The chapter ends with Xiao Ling presenting an object to the shadow, asking whether it belongs to it, and declaring that he now knows who it is.

Xiao Ling recognizes the original sacrificial victim, who willingly died in his younger sister’s place and later lured others into the site because he believed sacrifices protected families. Rather than destroy him with a dagger, Xiao Ling shares his memories of the land today to show that such sacrifices are no longer necessary, and the spirit apologizes. The students awaken in a classroom, mostly believing their supernatural ordeal was a shared dream, while one suspicious friend becomes determined to rescue Lu Huai from Xiao Ling after learning that Lu Huai works as his live-in assistant. Later, the powerful supernatural being freed from the seal appears and explains that there was no treasure there, then offers Xiao Ling—who is missing part of his soul and exists between life and death—a way out by abandoning humanity and joining them. Xiao Ling refuses, but the being gives his true name, Lixi, and leaves the invitation open in gratitude for his release. The chapter ends with a hidden observer relieved that a bird distracted attention from him, only for someone to ask what he is doing there.

Xiao Qing encounters a suspicious person hiding outside with binoculars, who claims to be birdwatching and hurriedly leaves, before visiting Xiao Ling and Lu Huai amid their bickering. She asks them to investigate rumors of people returning from the dead in Sangyu Town on behalf of an acquaintance whose family is involved. Xiao Ling initially hesitates because the trip seems unrelated to recovering his soul, but immediately accepts upon seeing the generous payment and covered expenses. Lu Huai insists on accompanying him to help if he collapses or his soul leaves his body, and Xiao Qing joins them as the intermediary. During their journey, a talking animal companion complains about being confined to a carrier in the pet-friendly carriage, and the chapter ends with an uneasy sense that something else is present onboard.

At the singing competition, the catlike host introduces the next contestant, Lu Huai. As the accompaniment begins, Lu Huai unleashes a performance described as demonic sounds piercing the ears. The judges appear somewhat moved, though the performance apparently leaves some unable to survive it. All the surviving judges vote to pass Lu Huai, and the host congratulates him on advancing.

While traveling with Lu Huai, Xueqiu, and Xiaoqing, Xiao Ling falls asleep and dreams of an unnervingly gentle, smiling Lu Huai in an otherwise empty vehicle surrounded by darkness. He wakes to learn that the others struggled to rouse him, and Lu Huai catches a three-headed, crow-like creature on his shoulder. The creature is identified as a dream-related yaoguai called Nueyu, apparently attracted by Xiao Ling’s dream, and they release it because it is still a baby and has harmed no one. Xiao Ling privately wonders whether Lu Huai’s ability to catch supernatural beings barehanded comes from absorbing a familiar earlier or from Xiao Ling’s own influence, and decides to keep observing him. They arrive in a seemingly peaceful town, where Xiao Ling buys four roasted sweet potatoes and asks the local vendor whether anything strange has happened recently.

Two investigators, posing as folklore students, find the townspeople evasive about strange local events before visiting Uncle Niu, whose nephew arranged their investigation. After a cow unexpectedly opens his gate, Uncle Niu welcomes them and explains the reported return of a girl presumed dead. In a flashback, the townspeople shun the girl because they believe she can curse people to death, and nobody wants to notify her during a flood evacuation. Niu goes to rescue her but hesitates when he finds her in danger of falling down a slippery cliff, fearing both for his safety and the supposed curse; she falls and is later declared dead after a search. Still blaming himself for the delay, he confirms that this same girl has now returned, and the chapter ends with one investigator asking him to repeat a particular statement.

The group learns that the girl who fell off a cliff over a decade ago was declared dead without her body ever being found, raising the possibility that she survived by falling into the nearby river. Uncle Niu insists that the girl he saw looks exactly as she did back then, and says her distinctive eyes and supernatural air resemble Xiaoling’s. Xiaoling and Xiaoqing decide to gather more information about the girl and the town’s secrets before visiting the house halfway up the mountain that Uncle Niu mentioned. Their investigation is interrupted by a commotion at the northern intersection, where they follow a crowd. The chapter ends with a woman revealing that the Wang family’s son has returned, even though he supposedly died in an accident last year.

A supposedly dead man returns to his mother, but the investigators recognize that he is merely an empty shell. They discover silk that fell from him and suspect a connection between his apparent resurrection, the symbolism of emerging from a cocoon, and Sangyu Town’s former silkworm industry, so Xiaoqing returns to the inn to research it. Meanwhile, Xiaoling investigates the mysterious girl mentioned by Uncle Niu and learns that people she names soon die, causing her family to abandon her and the townspeople to shun her. Lu Huai questions Xiaoling’s personal interest in the girl, especially his reaction to the description of her eyes, but Xiaoling evades the question and leaves angrily to eat alone. Xiaoling books a separate room to avoid Lu Huai, only to find it at the end of an unnaturally cold corridor, where his feline companion warns him not to turn around as he senses something behind him.

Fleeing a ghost, Xiao Ling begs Lu Huai to let him into his room and agrees to answer his earlier questions in exchange. A mountain spirit named Xiao Ba confronts them about investigating Shanshan, but apologizes after learning they are newcomers helping Uncle Niu discover whether she is alive or dead. Xiao Ba explains that Shanshan can see spirits and befriended them after being rejected by humans; her powerful protector, Luoxia, has been captured, and Shanshan is missing, possibly hidden away by Luoxia. At Xiao Ba’s request, the group follows him into the mountains the next day and discovers human-sized cocoons connected to the supposedly resurrected dead. Xiao Ba reveals that the cocoons formed when Shanshan’s powers went out of control after Luoxia’s capture, and the chapter ends as one cocoon begins to split open.

A cocoon releases a figure resembling Xiaoqing’s deceased older sister, Chunlan, raising questions about how Shanshan’s uncontrolled power creates these apparent revivals. Xiaoba explains that Luoxia once guarded the area as a guide versed in souls and related magic, prompting Xiaoling to eagerly support rescuing her in hopes of recovering their own soul. As the group takes Chunlan’s likeness back to the inn, Lu Huai privately warns Xiaoling to be wary of Xiaoqing’s intentions; Xiaoqing later insists the figure is only an empty shell and that forcibly bringing back the dead is wrong. Meanwhile, the mysterious man pressures the captive Luoxia to surrender Shanshan so he can drain her power and attempt resurrection, despite Luoxia explaining that her previous attempt left Shanshan trapped between life and death in an endless nightmare. He expects the spreading chaos to force Luoxia’s cooperation, while she silently hopes Xiaoba finds her before Shanshan’s power spirals further out of control.
